Report Details
Inspection Client: NUCOMER ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 1/10/2023
Violation Code: 78.88(e) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to submit an annual report to the Department identifying the compliance status of each well with the mechanical integrity requirements for structurally sound wells in compliance with 25 Pa. Code Section 78.73(c).
Violation ID: 981356
Permit API: 085-24042
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: West Salem Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/10/2023
Comments: Routine field inspection performed in late afternoon with cold, cloudy weather conditions, and 32 degrees. Last inspection performed on 3/20/17, more than 5 years ago. Wellhead is located in wooded forest area behind residence ~120' South of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility (photo #2). At the wellhead a pump jack is installed and open to well, lower left side production tubular valve closed to drip, lower production tubular right side valve is open to ports and plumbed to sales, valves to ports are closed, upper production tubular left is closed to ports and right side has closed valve to T-shaped union plumbed to sales/surface equipment with open main valve; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photos #3 and #4). Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead (photo #5). The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility and does not require a well label/marker (photo #2 and #5). Some trace to moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, pump jack, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility, one 100 bbl steel tank, and one 50 bbl poly tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #6). Valve open on main tubular feeding facility with cracked open valve to and from separator (photos #7 and #8). A 31-day production chart is present, with no clear markings just ink smear dated 5/2/22 (photo #9). A plumbed, in line drip and domestic house gas meter run is present at facility after the production recording chart apparatus (photos #7 and #8). Meter reading (photo #10). Well posting signage affixed to steel tank with all information about well and current Operator present, except the Operator contact address information (photo #11). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and tank. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 30 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 142 Mcf recorded over 365 days. This is an active, producing well.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-07-24 to Repsol Oil & Gas Usa Llc in Liberty Twp, Tioga county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Repsol Oil & Gas Usa Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-07-24
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 856826
Permit API: 117-21982
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-07-24
Comments: Wellhead painting on location, no other activity initially noted. Sitewide containment had been pulled up and rig mats were stacked. Many puddles were present on the pad; conductance readings in these puddles ranged from .7 to 1.4 mS/cm. Water was present in the area where the high conductance fluid had been noted during the frac; conductance reading was .98 mS/cm. I walked down the fill slope to the intercept trench and met Nick Shelman of Principal Enterprise. The intercept was nearly full of water and Nick was firing up the pump to move the water to the Baker tanks on the pad. Nick informed me that the pump was manned during the day and overnight if rain was expected. Conductivity of the water in the intercept was .55 mS/cm. The outlet to the sed trap had been filled in; water in the sed trap showed conductance of .35 mS/cm.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/21/2021 to CHIEF OIL & GAS LLC in Troy Twp, Bradford county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHIEF OIL & GAS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/21/2021
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 940013
Permit API: 015-23255
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/21/2021
Comments: I spoke with Mike Pettit and Nick Dunnett on site (both Resource Environmental Inc). They said MR Dirt performed the cleanup of the pad material affected by the ~10 gallon oil release last night. They excavated gravelly pad material and put it in the red dumpster, filling it about half way. Resource performed screening with a photoionization detector (PID) and visually inspected the area to confirm the cleanup. Resource got a 0.0 ppm reading, as did I (photo). Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22(a) Permanent Stabilization. I did not observe accelerated erosion or sedimentation during this inspection. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact; I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies today. Pooled water on the pad surface has electrical conductivity of 0.22-0.66 mS/cm with an Oakton PCSTestr 35. Air temp 37F JLP

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 2020-06-23
Comments: At 17:48 on Saturday (6/20/20), Doug Kepler reported a hose rupture on well pad D08-O that resulted in the discharge of 110-120 barrels of production fluid to containment. Doug Kepler reported about 8-10 barrels of fluid overflowed containment onto a gravel road. It was determined that the spill flowed for 3-4 minutes prior to being noted and then shut off. At the time of this inspection, the operator was in the process of removing the contaminated soil from the impacted area. The containment was vacuumed dry and then removed. A mini excavator and rolloff containers were brought on site. Screening was done of the impacted soil using a soil conductivity meter with a probe. It was determined that the production water flowed along the access road approximately 200-250 feet in a narrow band before exiting the road surface in a small depression. The operator had removed all the impacted soil in this stretch at the time of this inspection. They were loading their 11th container at this time. An excavation was developing deeper on the northeast side of the spill site, where elevated conductivity was noted several feet into the soil. The operator will continue to screen and remove soil today and for as long as necessary. Rolloff containers are being staged on the D08-O pad, which is just off the edge of the spill location. Further follow up of this spill location will be performed as necessary.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 982696
Permit API: 015-23717
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 1/24/2023
Comments: On 1/24/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Floydie well site. It was 34 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Snowfall had occurred in the last 48 hours, leaving approximately 4 inches on the ground. I was met on site by Justin Meyers who described current operations as follows: A Halliburton frac crew had finished the completion of four newly drilled wells on site and were in the process of removing the frac equipment from the site. The four newly completed wells have kill plugs installed and are waiting on plug drill outs. The six completed wells were still shut in at the time of the inspection. Justin accompanied me on the site inspection. I field tested some water puddles with two areas of the pad showing elevated conductance. A 6' x 10' x 1 1/2" water puddle outside of secondary containment on the south corner of the pad near the chemical additive area field tested at 11.93 mS conductance. I collected sample #9551-039 from this area for laboratory analysis. After the sample was pulled from the location, a vac truck sucked up the free liquid. Within 25 minutes, free liquid was witnessed in the same area, again testing at almost 12.0 mS. A 10' x 10' water puddle outside of secondary containment in the brine unloading area field tested at 4.90 mS conductance using an Oakton PCTS 50. This was in a larger muddy area. Using a Hanna Groline meter, I field tested multiple locations in the larger water/mud area that was approximately 35' x 20' x 1", the reading being 4000 uS which is the upper limit of the meter. I collected sample #9551-040 from the water puddle with the 4.90 mS conductance reading. Before leaving the site, I discussed the areas with elevated conductance readings with Chesapeake's Aaron Stredny. He said that they would continue sucking up the free liquid from the puddle in the south corner of the pad. He said that tomorrow, 1/25/2023, he would have personnel scrape and clean the brine unloading area and load the scraped material into containers for proper disposal.The site was covered with about four inches of snow so site stabilization could not be assessed during the inspection. PCSM is addressed on site by six infiltration berms that were covered with snow.Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 for the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface in the two areas of the pad.I left the site at 1545 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/10/2026 to VESSELS COAL GAS INC in Munster Township, Cambria county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: VESSELS COAL GAS INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/10/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8288603
Permit API: 021-20870
Unconventional: No
County: Cambria
Municipality: Munster Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/10/2026
Comments: On 9/10/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Gergely 1 well in Munster Township, Cambria County.This inspection was conducted in response to a referral from OGI Matt Woods (Inspection ID: 4268198 on 9/01/2026; Inspection ID: 4269845 on 9/03/2026). OGI Matt Woods requested that a WQS follow up because of potential surface pollution concerns regarding a plastic-lined pit observed during IR 4269845.This inspection is not evaluating compliance with Order 450586, as it is being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- No equipment related to production and/or well plugging operations was observed on site. The plastic-lined pit documented in IR 4269845 was not observed during this inspection (Photos 11 and 19). No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site at the time of inspection. No plugging monument was observed at the former location of the well. The API number and Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) were found on site (Photos 16 and 17).- The access road and well site remain heavily rutted, which appears to be caused by vehicles and machinery that were tracked-in for well plugging operations. Some mulch and seed was observed on site. However, the mulch and seed implemented on site is inadequate, as large portions of exposed soil are observable (Photos 12-15 and 20-21).- No perimeter Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls were observed on site. No E and S Restoration plan was observed on site during this inspection.Based on today's inspection, the violations issued in IR 4263564 against the heavy tire rutting and for failure to have the E and S/Restoration plan available on site will remain outstanding. An additional violation is being issued in this inspection for failure to implement adequate seed and temporary stabilization on areas that were disturbed by well plugging operations.The outstanding violations issued for failure to post the API number and operator's information on site are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.The Department requests that the Operator provide an electronic copy of the Control and Disposal Plan and provide clarification regarding the purpose of the plastic-lined pit observed during the time of IR 4269845, what it contained, and method of disposal used. Please provide this clarification no later than 9/29/2026. Additional violations may be forthcoming upon receipt and review of the clarification from the Operator.

Violation ID: 8264084

Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Date: 2/06/2026
Comments: On February 6, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the PF Eisaman South 43 Well Site (NOT previously approved on 6/6/2025) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 2/6/2026 (CTS 394994). Present during the inspection were operator representatives D.J Menas and Bruce Carpenter.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel. Site stabilization could not be assessed due to snow cover.At the time of inspection, there are 6 total wells on the well pad. All wells appeared equipped for production with a well tag present. No fluid leaks or spills were identified at the surface around any of the well heads or cellars. The GPUs appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Carpenter guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Carpenter the release occurred earlier in the morning on 2/6/2026 when a worker was filling a day tank in their truck with diesel from the diesel tank on the pad (photo 4). According to Mr. Carpenter, as the worker was filling the tank, they observed a leak from their tank was occurring. The worker immediately stopped pumping the diesel and pulled their truck forward. In doing so, a second smaller area of diesel release was created. According to Mr. Carpenter they are estimating 20 gallons of diesel was released on to the gravel well pad.The location of the initial release was directly adject to the onsite diesel tank (photo 5-8). The area of impacted material in this location was approximately 16 feet by 18 feet according to the operator. At the time of the inspection, the operator was actively excavating the impacted material in this area and placing it in into a roll off box.The location of where the additional diesel was released when the truck pulled forward was approximately 20 feet south of the onsite diesel tank (photo 10). The area of impacted material in this location was approximately 6 feet by 4 feet according to the operator.The Department was unable to obtain conductivity readings as the ground was frozen/heavily compacted. It was also difficult for the Department to discern any staining the release may have caused on the gravel well pad due to it actively snowing during the inspection, covering the area of the release.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation besubmitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the Eisaman 6H well for the release.

Comments: On August 19, 2024 the Department (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of State Game Lands 51B1 Well located in Dunbar Township, Fayette County, where violations were continued for a release from production equipment inside the green shed.At the time of this inspection, Minor rutting is developing in the access road as it enters the well site; therefore, the Department recommends the operator continue to monitor and maintain the access road as necessary in order to prevent any erosion and sedimentation events from occurring. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniformand adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the area where a production tank had previously been placed. The DEP recommends this area be seeded and mulched. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection.Two production tanks within secondary containment were observed. One of the production tanks appeared rusted but no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed. However, the tank's secondary containment was nearly full of fluid. The DEP recommends that the containment be drained, fluid be disposed of properly, and in accordance with regulations. The well tag was present at the time of this inspection. A well tag was found on the ground near wellhead. The Dept recommends the Operator permanently affix the well tag in accordance with 3211(h) . There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. No fluid discharges were observed coming from the production tank near the wellhead onsite, however, the production tanks lid was cracked in half and open and there appeared to be a high level of fluid in this production tank. The DEP recommends the Operator replace the lid on this production tank and properly dispose of the contents within this tank to prevent a potential release. The production tank near the green shed had a hose inside the secondary containment extending out onto the ground. It appears that water in the secondary containment is being discharged to the ground as the secondary containment is at capacity. The Department recommends the removal of this excess fluid in accordance with current regulations to accommodate any potential releases that may occur. Inside the green shed located on this well site, a compressor station as well as various barrels with various unknown substances not in containment were observed. Some barrels were heavily rusted and staining in the gravel was observed underneath them as well as under the GPU and production equipment. The Department request the Operator provide information on what exactly is in the drums and what they are being used for. The Department request that this information be provided with the NOV response. The Department also recommends that the Operator remove all equipment/supplies not necessary for production.Inside the green shed, the spill that was previously observed in inspection reports 3743832 and 3808945 remains. In this green shed, the spill appears to be an oily like petroleum substance on the ground. The DEP again recommends that the Operator remediate the areas as necessary in accordance with the Department's Spill Policy. The DEP again requests the operator evaluate the releases that have occurred and provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. The GPU unit (not in secondary containment) in this green shed had no observable active leaks or discharge.Based on today's inspection violations for the spill shall remain outstanding along with failure to have the well tag permanently affixed to the wellhead.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/11/2022 to PA GEN ENERGY CO LLC in Keating Twp, Potter county. 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PA GEN ENERGY CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/11/2022
Violation Code: 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
Violation ID: 955459
Permit API: 105-21845
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Keating Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/11/2022
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the PGE – Hancock Pad A located in Keating Twp, Potter Co. on 5/12/22 @1210 hours in response to a reported release of approximately 10 barrels of brine to the pad surface (CID#364034). The weather was 73 degrees, sunny, winds ENE@3mph. Mr. Chad Earley, PGE HSE Supervisor and Mr. Matt Covine, PGE Completions Consultant were present onsite for the inspection. Mr. Earley stated a cement truck was parked in secondary containment yesterday during the previous days plugging activities. A brine solution was spilled into the secondary containment from the truck. At the end of yesteday’s plugging activities, the secondary containment was "almost full" of the brine solution. The brine solution was left in the secondary containment overnight. Mr. Earley stated when Mr. Covine arrived onsite the next morning, there was less brine solution in the secondary containment and visible staining and fluid on the pad surface. Mr. Earley estimates 10 barrels of fluid was released to the pad surface. I screened the fluid remaining in the secondary containment with an Oakton Multiparameter meter. The field conductivity was measured at 18.8mS/cm. Damp areas around the secondary containment were screened with a Groline soil conductivity meter and found to be >4.0mS/cm. Two vac trucks arrived onsite to remove the fluid remaining in the secondary containment as well as the brine solution remaining in the two water tanks adjacent to the spill area. The secondary containment responsible for the release was lifted with a telehandler and the underside examined. The Secondary containment appeared to have a seam that was not properly sealed, this allowed fluid to leak from the bottom of the containment. The visibly impacted area was estimated to cover ~20’ long x 12’ wide. As material was excavated and placed into a lined rolloff waste container, a clay layer was encountered approximately 14" below the pad surface. Mr. Earley screened the clay material with a field conductivity meter and found the material measured <500uS/cm. Mr. Earley stated the clay later appeared to be a barrier for further infiltration of the brine solution. Mr. Earley also stated the brine solution appeared to have laterally migrated under the brine tank containment adjacent to the excavated spill area. Mr. Earley stated their plan was to excavate the 12’ x 20’ impacted area, while field screening, to ensure all impacted areas are identified. PGE would then line the area with plastic and backfill with clean gravel to accommodate completion of the plugging activity. Mr. Earley stated PGE would then have the tanks and their containment removed to further screen the area under the tanks and remove any additional impacted material. I requested Mr. Earley email me pictures of today's completed cleanup activities and provided my contact information. Due to the reported volume of the release being greater than 42 gallons the operator must demonstrate attainment of one or more of the standards established by Act 2 and Chapter 250. This incident is referred to the DEP Cleanups Program for Follow-up. Violations of the following regulations are cited against the Hancock Pad A 2741 Well (API#105-21845) at this time: 25 Pa Code 78a.64(b) 25 Pa Code 78a.64(f) CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 I departed the site at 1440 hours.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 5/16/2023 at 0902 hours. The inspection was conducted to follow-up on remedial activities occurring onsite related to a release from 4/6/2023.Sumps constructed as part of the remedial efforts in the excavated/impacted areas remain in place and continue to have collected fluids recovered. All excavated areas remain exposed and were mostly dry today. The southern stormwater conveyance channel that was impacted as a result of the release from 4/6/2023 remains excavated (photos #2 and 3). The impacted stormwater control basin was empty and dry today (photo #4). Impacted material excavated as a result of the release remains staged onsite. Portions of the impacted material are held within lined residual waste containers on secondary containment and portions are held directly on secondary containment and covered with liner. The residual waste containers are in the process of being trucked offsite. Pooled water held within the impacted/excavated area located just west of the initial release point (photo #7) was field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at ~900us/cm today. Water held in the northern stormwater conveyance channel was field measured for EC at ~700us/cm today (photo #5). Discussion to excavate further along the produced water flow-line as explained in inspection record #3543714 has been completed and soil characterization samples have been collected. Violations cited against API #015-23733 on 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time. No additional violations are noted at this time. I departed the site at 1030 hours.

Violation ID: 8277972
Permit API: 015-23981
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wysox Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/15/2026
Comments: On 02/26/2026 Expand representative Steven Moyer reported a discovered release onsite (CTS #395411). He stated "there was a hole in containment. An unknown amount of frack water mixed with stormwater on pad." On 02/27/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of the Wygrala Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. The area of the reported release is estimated to be an area of 75x150. Within the 75x150 area the elevated conductivity of the soil varies between 0-4 mS/cm. The cause of the release was due to a ripped seam in the pad wide containment.On 06/15/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of. The weather was 59 degrees and partly sunny. Rain fell on the pad within the last 24 hours. I arrived at 0900 hours. The site appeared stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation onsite. Pooled fluids on the pad surface were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 505-892 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment. There was a water truck onsite during the inspection. There were six temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment. There were five wells capable of producing onsite. Each well was properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. Due to the unknown quantity of the release this has been referred to ECB for Act 2 compliance.Based on the reported release (CTS #395411) the following violations remain open against API #015-23981:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed at 0945 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/24/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/24/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 973252
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/24/2022
Comments: On October 24, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. DEP spoke with Profrac Company Man Mike Reel and he said they were fracking the 1005H well at the time of inspection. The DEP observed multiple areas of staining adjacent to the containment for the fracking rig. The areas were screened for conductivity with a soil conductivity meter and two areas resulted in over range conductivity readings. The upper limit of the soil conductivity meter is 4.0 mS/cm. The first area is adjacent to the frack pumps off the east side of containment. This area of high conductivity is about 12' x 20'. The second area is adjacent to 1 frac tank and 2 gas buster tanks. This area of high conductivity is about 10'x10'. Soil sample 0651-139 was collected from the 10'x10' area. The volume of this spill is unknown because it is uncertain how much was spilled under the frack rig containment. The DEP pointed out the previously mentioned areas to Mr. Reel and he said he would have someone begin scraping up the areas immediately. DEP then placed a phone call to STL Resources Seth Rodriguez to inform him of the findings from the inspection. The DEP recommends assessing the area of elevated conductivity and updating DEP of the findings. Due to the unknown volume of the spill, the DEP recommends pursuing an Act 2 remediation. The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad on January 8, 2022. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. This water is being pumped into frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter in either of the stormwater vaults. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 22.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 22.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 25.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 26.2 uS/cm. Seep 1, 1a, and 3 were dry and could not be screened. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 31.7 uS/cm. Seep 4 was not screened due to the current condition of the seep screening area. This area is being driven through by ATVs checking on the freshwater waterline for the Sturgis South stimulation. The area is constantly being driven through to refuel the pumps on the waterline. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 24.7 uS/cm. The infiltration berms 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, and 11 along the access road are well vegetated and appear to be functioning correctly. Infiltration berms 1, 4, 6, 7, and 9 along the access road are vegetated but, the areas that are holding water have little vegetation and do not appear to be functioning correctly. Infiltration berm 1 off the northwest corner of the pad appears to be holding water and not functioning correctly. Infiltration berm 2 off the northwest corner of the pad and the infiltration berm off the southwest corner of the pad are lacking vegetation in the infiltration area. The DEP recommends working on the infiltration berms that are not functioning correctly and reseeding the infiltration berms that are lacking vegetation to prevent an erosion event. The areas of staining along with the elevated levels of conductivity outside of containment on the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b). Additional violations could be assessed pending results from the soil sample collected. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227 and 3306834

Inspection Date: 08/19/2020
Comments: On 08/19/2020 DEP representatives John Ciccone and Korey Starkey (Water Quality Specialist) conducted an incident inspection on Chesapeake's Ferraro location at 1000 hours. This inspection was in response to a spill notification (CID # 351908) received the early morning of 08/19/2020. The spill notification stated that at 0400 hours, a gas kick resulted in a release of 2.5 barrels of oil based mud from the well head. Eric Hottenstein (Chesapeake) estimated that 1.5 barrels sprayed on containment and 1 barrel sprayed off containment.At the time of arrival (1000 hours), we met with Eric Hottenstein at the pad entrance. Mr. Hottenstein explained that crews were currently mustered outside and that lines were shut-in. At approximately 1015 hours, Jon Zwetzig (Chesapeake Field Safety Representative) met with us and stated we were allowed back onsite along the perimeter of the pad. Mr. Zwetzig and Mr. Hottenstein led us toward the southern edge of the pad where the oil based mud sprayed off containment. From the point of the spraying event to the edge of containment was approximately 100' (photo # 2, 3). An additional 60' of vegetation had been excavated from the southern edge of the pad out toward the tree line (photo # 5). The gas kick took place while drilling the 5H well according to Mr. Zwetzig.According to Mr. Hottenstein, the majority of the sprayed oil based mud was captured by the dense vegetation off of the southern edge of the pad, with visually minimal oil based mud making contact with the ground (photo # 13). A dark staining was visually observed on the vegetation along the existing tree line that remained to be excavated (photo # 7, 8, 10, 13) and the smell of oil was heavy along the impacted treeline. Mr. Hottenstein stated that Chesapeake plans to continue excavating the impacted vegetation and then soil samples are to be taken from the roughly 60' x 60' excavated location (photo # 12). Sampling is to be conducted by Creston Environmental. Excavated vegetation and materials are being staged within containers at the Mad Dog lcoation, where additional plastic liner is being laid down for containment.Mr. Hottenstein stated that once excavation and soil sampling is completed, the excavated grounds will be hydroseeded and additional silt sock will be laid down gradient in order to mitigate any potential erosion and sedimentation.Mr. Hottenstein stated that Chesapeake will be pursuing Act 2 remediation.The release of a regulated substance to the ground surface is in violation of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and Chapter 78a.56(a). Due to an undetermined amount of regulated substance being released to the ground surface, please refer to 78a.66 regarding remediating releases of regulated substances on well sites.We departed the site at 1100 hours.

Comments: On March 9, 2026, the Department conducted a Routine Partial Inspection of Oil and Gas Mgmt's Armstrong 2 well located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. The Department's assessment of the shared portion of this access road as well as the direct portion of this access road can be found in IR 4155454At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Armstrong 2 well site to be overgrown with vegetation, the Department recommends the Operator maintain the vegetation within the well site to ensure the well site remains accessible. A well tag was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted gas well with all required information posted on it and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the surface of the gas well at this time. A heavily rusted production tank was also observed on site and connected for production, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this tank at this time. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tank to ensure the corrosion does not worsen resulting in a release. Based on today's inspection, Violations are being issued at this time for the heavily rusted production equipment due to their corrosion posing the risk of a spill and/or release.
